Definition: properly, to incline; by implication, to decline (of the slanting rays of evening); specifically, to pitch a tent; gen. to encamp (for abode or siege)
BiblicalUsage: Chanah is pitching camp, and the wilderness is full of it. Israel encamped before Pi-hahiroth by the sea, and wherever the cloud abode, there the children of Israel pitched their tents. After the Jordan they encamped at Gilgal and kept the passover, and the psalmist says that though a host should encamp against him, his heart shall not fear.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe encamping is the Bible's picture of a people who live by God's leading and not their own map. They pitched where the cloud stopped and moved when it lifted. I hold that my own life works the same way: I camp where He puts me, and I do not fear the host camped across the valley.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea; Circumcision and Passover at Gilgal
